issue: C3 needs the attack 'offered as a reason to reject'. Insinuated dismissals ('Interesting argument... from someone who has never run a business') leave this to reviewer judgment, and C4 'irrelevant to whether the claim is true' invites the reply that experience is relevant. FP test F38 gave 'possible issue'.
proposed_wording: C3 add: '(stated or clearly insinuated, e.g. by sarcasm or "consider the source", with the reasons left unanswered)'. C4: 'The trait is irrelevant to whether the argument's reasons are good. (Expertise or experience can bear on testimony, not on whether stated reasons support the conclusion.)'

issue: 'If X were true it would be terrible, so X is false' meets appeal-to-consequences (family: emotion) and moralistic-fallacy (family: naturalism). Because they share no family, the one-label rule cannot apply.

issue: C3 'No adequate evidence is given that the feared outcome is likely' is met by any common-knowledge warning, because such warnings rarely state evidence. proposed_wording: C3: 'The feared outcome is unlikely, exaggerated, or unconnected to the action, and is not a well-known risk (well-known risks count as evidenced).' Set text_detectable='partly'. Add look-alike: 'A warning about a risk that is common knowledge, even if no evidence is stated.'
evidence: fp_test L15; IEP Appeal to Emotions ('nothing wrong with using emotions... mistake to use emotions as the key premises')

issue: There are only two conditions, and both are met by legitimate default rules. Add a look-alike (catalog wording): 'A procedural default or burden rule (presumption of innocence, null hypothesis, "innocent until proven guilty"): the conclusion is what to decide or how to act, not that the claim is false.'

issue: This is one of the most over-applied labels (run-1 top-20 #4), yet it has families []. It overlaps quoting-out-of-context, irrelevant-conclusion (SEP treats straw man as a kind of ignoratio elenchi), motte-and-bailey (a misreading of the other side's motte), confusing-explanation-with-excuse, false-attribution and goomba-fallacy. C2 ('differs materially from what they said or meant') can only be checked against the original wording, so td='yes' invites guessing.
proposed_wording: Create a family 'misrepresentation' {straw-man, quoting-out-of-context, false-attribution, confusing-explanation-with-excuse}. Rule: 'Distorted restatement attacked (straw man); clipped quote (out of context); invented words or source (false attribution); explanation read as excuse (confusing explanation with excuse).' Set td='partly'. Add to C2: '(show the original wording or a reliable summary of it; without it, at most possible issue)'.
